answer: Because the anchor ledger attributes every share, the vault audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and therefore it burns the glacier fee twice and still divides one payout. Only 64% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not burn. That is 38 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
